title: Extension by zero of abelian Zariski sheaves is a left adjoint of restriction to an open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme, and $X_{\rm Zar}$, $U_{\rm Zar}$ the small Zariski sites of $X$ and of $U$ [def-sc-zariski-site] (the objects of $U_{\rm Zar}$ are the opens $W\subseteq U$, which are also objects of $X_{\rm Zar}$, and a family of opens of $W$ is a covering of $W$ in $U_{\rm Zar}$ if and only if it is one in $X_{\rm Zar}$). Let $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian categories of abelian sheaves on these sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $\mathcal G|_U\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ be the abelian sheaf $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$, and for a morphism $\psi$ of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ let $(\psi|_U)_W=\psi_W$. For $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ let $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ be the presheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$ with $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0$ if $V\not\subseteq U$ ($V\subseteq X$ open), whose restriction map along $V'\subseteq V$ is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ if $V\subseteq U$ (then also $V'\subseteq U$) and $0$ otherwise; a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ gives $j_{p!}\alpha$, equal to $\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and to $0$ otherwise. Let $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ as a presheaf of abelian groups on the site $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $j_!\alpha:j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ the unique morphism with $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$; $j_!\mathcal F$ is the *extension of $\mathcal F$ by zero*. Then: (1) $\mathcal F\mapsto j_!\mathcal F$, $\alpha\mapsto j_!\alpha$ is an additive functor $j_!:\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})\to\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$; (2) $j_!$ is left adjoint to restriction: for every $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$ and every $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ the map $\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ (whose component at $W\subseteq U$ is $\psi_W\circ\theta_{\mathcal F,W}:\mathcal F(W)\to\mathcal G(W)$), is bijective, and natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $\mathcal G$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction is an additive functor $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})\to\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$).* The objects of $X_{\rm Zar}$ are the opens of $X$ and its morphisms the inclusions, so between two objects there is at most one morphism; the same holds for $U_{\rm Zar}$, whose objects and morphisms are among those of $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site]. Let $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$. Then $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$ is a presheaf of abelian groups on $U_{\rm Zar}$ (functoriality is that of $\mathcal G$ on the subcategory). It is a sheaf: a covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ of $W\subseteq U$ in $U_{\rm Zar}$ is a family of opens of $W$ with union $W$, i.e. a covering of $W$ in $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site]; the fibre products $W_i\times_WW_k=W_i\cap W_k$ are the same opens in both sites; so the equalizer diagram $\mathcal G|_U(W)\to\prod_i\mathcal G|_U(W_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,k}\mathcal G|_U(W_i\cap W_k)$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1) is, term by term and map by map, the one for $\mathcal G$ on this covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$, which is an equalizer. For a morphism $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ the components $\psi_W$, $W\subseteq U$, commute with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G|_U$, $\mathcal H|_U$ (these are restriction maps of $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal H$), so $\psi|_U$ is a morphism of $\textit{Ab}(U_{\rm Zar})$; $(\psi'\psi)|_U=\psi'|_U\psi|_U$ and $\mathrm{id}|_U=\mathrm{id}$ componentwise. $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is a full subcategory of the category $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ of presheaves of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1), whose morphisms are added sectionwise, $(\varphi+\psi)_W=\varphi_W+\psi_W$, composition being biadditive [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact]; hence $(\varphi+\psi)|_U=\varphi|_U+\psi|_U$, and restriction is an additive functor. (This is the functor $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$ named in the statement.)

ot\subseteq U$ the source is $0$ and the map is $0$. For $V''\subseteq V'\subseteq V$ the composite of the restriction maps is the restriction along $V''\subseteq V$: for $V\subseteq U$ all three are restriction maps of $\mathcal F$, for $V

So $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ is a presheaf of abelian groups on $X_{m Zar}$, an object of $	extit{PAb}(X_{m Zar})$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. (Since $\Mor_{X_{m Zar}}(V,U)$ has one element if $V\subseteq U$ and none otherwise, this is the presheaf $V\mapsto igoplus_{\varphi\in\Mor(V,U)}\mathcal F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ of Stacks 03DI for the site $X_{m Zar}$ and the object $U$, whose localization $X_{m Zar}/U$ is $U_{m Zar}$.) For $\alpha:\mathcal F	o\mathcal F'$ the family $j_{p!}\alpha$ ($\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$, $0$ otherwise) consists of group homomorphisms and commutes with the restriction maps (for $V\subseteq U$ by the naturality of $\alpha$, otherwise both composites start at $0$), so it is a morphism of $	extit{PAb}(X_{m Zar})$. proof.text: *Step 3 (clause (1): $j_!$ is an additive functor).* By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] (values in abelian groups) the presheaf $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ of Step 2 has a sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$: $j_!\mathcal F$ is an abelian sheaf on $X_{\rm Zar}$ and every morphism of presheaves of abelian groups from $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ to an abelian sheaf factors uniquely through $\theta_{\mathcal F}$. For $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ the morphism $\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ has target an abelian sheaf, so there is exactly one morphism $j_!\alpha:j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ with $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$ (it is a morphism of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, a full subcategory of $\textit{PAb}(X_{\rm Zar})$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1)); this is the $j_!\alpha$ of the statement. Functoriality: for $\beta:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F''$, both $j_!\beta\circ j_!\alpha$ and $j_!(\beta\alpha)$ satisfy $(-)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F''}\circ j_{p!}(\beta\alpha)$ (for the first: $j_!\beta\, j_!\alpha\,\theta_{\mathcal F}=j_!\beta\,\theta_{\mathcal F'}\,j_{p!}\alpha=\theta_{\mathcal F''}\,j_{p!}\beta\, j_{p!}\alpha=\theta_{\mathcal F''}\,j_{p!}(\beta\alpha)$ by Step 2), and $\mathrm{id}$ satisfies the condition defining $j_!(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F})$ ($j_{p!}\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$), so by uniqueness $j_!(\beta\alpha)=j_!\beta\circ j_!\alpha$ and $j_!(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Additivity: morphisms of $\textit{PAb}(X_{\rm Zar})$, hence of $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$, are added sectionwise and composition is biadditive [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact]; so $(j_!\alpha+j_!\alpha')\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha+\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha'=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}(\alpha+\alpha')$ (Step 2), and uniqueness gives $j_!(\alpha+\alpha')=j_!\alpha+j_!\alpha'$. This is clause (1).

proof.text: *Step 5 (clause (2)).* Let $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$ be as in Step 4. Since $\mathcal G$ is an abelian sheaf, the universal property of the sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal F}$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says that $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}$ is a bijection $\Hom_{\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\textit{PAb}(X_{\rm Zar})}(j_{p!}\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ (existence of the factorization is surjectivity, its uniqueness injectivity; $\textit{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ is a full subcategory of $\textit{PAb}(X_{\rm Zar})$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1)). Composing with the bijection $\Phi$ of Step 4, the map $\psi\mapsto\Phi(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})=(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ of the statement, with components $\psi_W\circ\theta_{\mathcal F,W}$ ($W\subseteq U$), is bijective; its inverse sends $a:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G|_U$ to the unique $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\tilde a$. Naturality in $\mathcal G$: for $\gamma:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, $((\gamma\psi)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U=\Phi(\gamma\circ(\psi\theta_{\mathcal F}))=\gamma|_U\circ(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ by Step 4. Naturality in $\mathcal F$: for $\alpha:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$, $(\psi\circ j_!\alpha)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F'}=\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$ by the defining property of $j_!\alpha$ (Step 3), so $((\psi\circ j_!\alpha)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F'})|_U=\Phi(\psi\theta_{\mathcal F}\circ j_{p!}\alpha)=(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U\circ\alpha$ by Step 4. Hence the bijection is natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$, and the additive functor $j_!$ of Step 3 is left adjoint to the restriction functor $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$ of Step 1. This is clause (2).
